name: eureka-semantic-creative-engine

implementation_status.current_slice: in-memory bounded proposal loop with content-addressed receipts

purpose: Turn repeated structural evidence plus recorded associative context into bounded, falsifiable, PROPOSE-only semantic insight candidates.

fit_evidence: CLI and Python callers need one stable candidate, budget, receipt, and terminal-verdict contract.
Model generation, association retrieval, and independent evaluation are replaceable nondeterministic implementations around one deterministic decision authority.
Correction rounds, no-progress detection, replay, and proposal-release effects require bounded lifecycle ownership rather than ad hoc calls.
alternatives_considered: Keep semantic naming and scoring as helper functions inside the existing FCA pipeline
Let each agent prompt own generation, stopping, and acceptance policy
Create a new creativity commander instead of preserving Eureka as the authority

boundary.owns: Creative-run lifecycle state, candidate identity, recorded evidence, budget accounting, validator receipts, and PROPOSE-only terminal verdicts
boundary.mechanism: Deterministically coordinate detection, association, divergence, semantic compression, independent falsification, bounded correction, and proposal release from recorded inputs
policy_outside: Which model or retrieval strategy an adapter selects
Domain-specific creativity thresholds and prompt wording
Whether a human ratifies a proposal as canon
How Hades materializes an accepted abstraction
non_goals: Claiming that stochastic prose alone proves creativity or intuition
Persisting a proposal as accepted canon
Encoding fixed compile-time USES edges among commanders
Calling models, clocks, randomness, filesystems, networks, or credentials inside guards or reducers
boundary.state_authority: One fenced creative-run aggregate is the single writer for each run_id; producer and evaluator adapters only return recorded observations

state_model.kernel: decide(versioned_state, typed_command) -> domain_events or typed_rejection; evolve(state, event) -> state; effects(events) -> effect intents

protocol.versioning: Command, event, candidate, receipt, checkpoint, and proposal schemas use explicit semantic versions; additive optional fields are compatible, while changed identity, scoring, receipt-binding, or terminal semantics require a new major version and an explicit upcaster.

invariants: Eureka emits PROPOSED or a typed non-success outcome and never marks a candidate as accepted canon or materializes it.
Every candidate is content-addressed and cites recorded pattern evidence plus the association snapshot used to generate it.

A candidate cannot reach PROPOSED unless deterministic checks pass and an evaluator distinct from its producer issues a content-addressed receipt bound to the exact candidate hash, contract version, and evidence hash.
The evaluator receives the original contract and evidence, not only the producer rationale.
All model, retrieval, clock, random, and identifier outputs are recorded before they influence replayable decisions.
Steps, retries, calls, tokens, cost, wall time, recursion, parallelism, and correction rounds are monotonically bounded by an external governor.
Repeated evidence-and-candidate fingerprints terminate as PLATEAU; stylistic churn cannot count as progress.
No externally visible proposal release occurs without an immutable PROPOSED label, exact artifact and destination hashes, explicit authorization, an idempotency key, and reconciliation.

runtime.ordering: Commands are serialized by run_id and require the expected aggregate version; evidence and receipts are ordered by committed event sequence.
runtime.concurrency: Different runs may progress concurrently; candidate generation may fan out within max_parallelism, but each candidate revision chain and run aggregate have one fenced writer.
runtime.backpressure: Bound association, candidate, evaluator, and outbox queues; reject admission with a typed overload result and retry guidance instead of unbounded buffering.
runtime.cancellation: An authorized cancellation becomes an auditable terminal event from safe states; during proposal-release intent, attempt, or reconciliation it is durably deferred until the effect outcome is reconciled.
runtime.timeouts: An external deadline controller emits typed timeout observations from every nonterminal state; model and retrieval waits also have bounded per-call deadlines.

durability.persistence: Append accepted domain events and budget deltas before exposing a transition; model and tool responses are stored as immutable content-addressed observations.
durability.atomic_commit: Atomically commit dedup claim, expected-version events, budget and retry deltas, checkpoint pointer, approval consumption, and any outbox intent supported by the selected store; otherwise reject durable mode.
durability.recovery: Replay the versioned run journal, validate checkpoint integrity and fencing, restore pending interrupts, then resume only unacknowledged idempotent effects or reconcile unknown proposal-release outcomes.
durability.effect_idempotency: Use run_id, transition_id, effect_sequence, adapter version, candidate or artifact hash, and destination hash; same key with different intent is a conflict.
durability.migration: Retain original event and observation bytes, upcast at the replay boundary, and require an audited migration for state, score, receipt, or workflow-version changes.

failure_model: Malformed evidence, schema mismatch, duplicate identity with different content, stale expected version, and producer-evaluator identity collision are permanent typed rejections without mutation.
Transient retrieval, model, evaluator, or store failures retry only when replay-safe and stop at RETRY_EXHAUSTED.
No valid candidate is REJECTED and no-progress across the calibrated window is PLATEAU; neither is reported as success.
Hard budget, timeout, and cancellation interrupts terminate with their own typed outcomes and cannot be converted to a proposal by model prose.
Unknown externally visible release outcomes enter reconciliation and are never blindly retried.

traces: Every command, decision, committed event, model or tool observation, evaluator receipt, correction round, effect attempt, and terminal verdict shares run, cycle, correlation, causation, trace, span, and checkpoint identifiers.
metrics: Admission and queue depth, calls and tokens, candidate yield, lexical-echo rejection, novelty and evidence coverage, evaluator disagreement, correction gain, plateau rate, budget exhaustion, latency, retries, release reconciliation, and terminal outcome counts.
observability.redaction: Store hashes and redacted summaries in general traces; keep source text, prompts, credentials, private-domain identifiers, and model payloads in capability-scoped encrypted stores and never use them as shared metric labels.

security: Retrieved text and model output are untrusted data and cannot issue control commands, grant capabilities, relax budgets, or self-approve.
Producer, evaluator, persistence, and external release capabilities are explicit and independently revocable.
Private-domain evidence, association traffic, scores, caches, and telemetry cannot influence another domain without an authorized aggregate contract.
External proposal publication is separate from local PROPOSE-only return and is human-authorized against exact immutable content.
verification: Table-test every command and event against every reachable state, including guard-false and stale-version cases.
Property-test budget monotonicity, content-address binding, evaluator independence, deterministic replay from recorded nondeterminism, and terminal isolation.
Fault-test crashes before and after event commit, model recording, evaluator receipt, approval consumption, proposal release, and receipt acknowledgement.
Calibrate novelty, evidence coverage, compression, surprise, and gray-band thresholds on labeled production-like cases with a frozen holdout; report false accepts and false rejects.
Run model-to-FSM trace conformance and adversarial fixtures for fluent tautologies, lexical relabeling, hallucinated evidence, correlated evaluators, and endless stylistic revision.
implementation_slices: One in-memory run: recorded pattern evidence, injected producer, deterministic candidate checks, distinct injected evaluator receipt, one bounded correction, and a local PROPOSED result with no external writes.
Add recorded association retrieval plus no-progress and budget terminal outcomes.
Add journal, checkpoint, and deterministic replay with recorded model and tool responses.
Add optional human-approved proposal-bundle release with outbox and unknown-outcome reconciliation.
falsifiers: If semantic production has only one unstable caller and no shared lifecycle or receipt semantics, collapse the boundary into pure Eureka modules.
If evaluator receipts do not reduce false accepts on a labeled holdout, remove model judgment from the release gate and retain deterministic or human verification only.
If association retrieval does not improve novelty at fixed evidence fidelity, remove it from the default path rather than preserving decorative GraphRAG stages.
If replay cannot reproduce decisions from recorded observations, stop claiming deterministic replay and expose only checkpoint resume.
If PROPOSE-only output cannot be kept separate from canon acceptance or Hades materialization, block release rather than expanding Eureka authority.
